correctness.rationale: Exact recursion enumerates all 65,536 vertex masks; independent subset/zeta-transform enumeration agrees at every mask and parameter. Reproducible element matchings on every nonempty face yield one critical zero-cell and 9,36,84,122,102,29,1 critical cells exclusively in dimensions 1,3,5,7,9,11,13. Every directed Hasse edge is generated and all nodes removed by exhaustive topological sorting, independently certifying acyclicity. Standard discrete-Morse theory therefore gives integral sphere wedges. For k>=9 alpha(P4 Cartesian P4)=8 makes a simplex. Finite exhaustion is a complete proof for this specified finite object, not a claimed infinite-range computational proof.

originality.rationale: The previously published 2022 numerical homology table contains the ranks 84,122,102,29, so no novelty is attributed to those ranks. The new mathematical assertion is an explicit perfect acyclic matching for each interior parameter 4–7 and the resulting integral homotopy wedges. The full 2026 motivating paper states this kind of higher-parameter square-sequence conclusion only as a conjecture; its existing all-parameter result is for edge-only attachments, not the present full rectangular grid. Published index results on 3-robust grids and much shorter square-sequence graphs cannot imply the stated 4×4 all-parameter classification. Residual risk is that the 2022 authors may have computed unpublished perfect matchings.
residual_risks: Betti counts are old and explicitly credited, not original. The older table authors mention lexicographic Morse matchings and may possess unpublished complete matching certificates for the same grid.
No general theorem for larger grids; no inference that the broader 2026 conjecture is resolved.
Unindexed or inaccessible equivalent homotopy-level work could affect priority; no independent audit performed.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves the higher-parameter, corner-gluing homotopy question on the canonical full 4×4 grid across all four nontrivial interior k values. It upgrades older Betti-number data to explicit integral homotopy types and provides a complete reproducible acyclic matching rather than simply reporting another known invariant. It verifies a specific natural finite case of the 2026 square-sequence wedge conjecture, while not claiming any general solution.
